summary: io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/io-wq: save worker type before dropping its reference

io_wq_cancel_tw_create() inspects cb->func after calling
io_worker_cancel_cb(). For an existing worker, that call can drop the
last worker reference and wake io_worker_exit(). If the canceling task
is preempted, the worker can be unlinked and freed by kfree_rcu() before
the callback function is inspected. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free
read in this path.

Save whether the callback belongs to an unpublished continuation worker
while its reference is still held, then use the saved result for the
conditional free. This preserves the existing accounting and frees only
the worker allocated for the canceled continuation.

summary: io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: defer foreign io-wq enqueues to task_work

An IOPOLL ring without DEFER_TASKRUN can be reaped by a task other than
the one that submitted the I/O. If a polled request is marked
REQ_F_REISSUE, io_free_batch_list() calls io_queue_iowq() with the
original tctx. Ordinary task exit can tear down tctx->io_wq after
draining only the tracked requests. The live request pins the task, but
not its io-wq, so the foreign task can race io_wq_put_and_exit() and
enqueue through a freed or NULL queue.

Forward foreign userspace enqueues to the owning task before accessing
tctx->io_wq. Use a dedicated task_work callback so reissues still go
straight to io-wq, and fail them if task_work is running in cancellation
mode. Preserve the existing PF_KTHREAD cancellation path. This also
covers the other callers of io_queue_iowq() without changing the
worker-owned enqueue path.

summary: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit

io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit.
The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a
SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up
doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until
someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64
closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from
being freed, for everyone.

Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it
gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a
second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread,
and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring,
rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash
is refcounted.

summary: io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/cancel: drop sqd->lock while SQPOLL waits

An exiting SQPOLL thread calls io_uring_cancel_generic() with sqd->lock
held, and keeps it across cond_resched() and the sleep until nothing is
in flight anymore. A zero-copy send notification can't be canceled and
stays pending as long as the peer doesn't read, so the lock is held for
as long as a user cares to. io_ring_exit_work() needs it to park the
thread, and so do IORING_REGISTER_IOWQ_AFF and IOWQ_MAX_WORKERS. With
64 such rings sharing the thread, every iou_exit slot sleeps on the lock
and no ring gets freed for anyone.

Drop the lock around cond_resched() and the sleep, like the main loop of
the thread does. Each walk of ctx_list is still under one hold, and
nothing is kept across the unlock. The thread drops its io-wq, frees its
tctx and clears sqd->thread under one hold after the loop, so whoever
holds the lock and finds sqd->thread set can still use them.

[axboe: adapted to the schedule_timeout() based loop]

summary: io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/poll: cancel all matching requests in one pass

With IORING_ASYNC_CANCEL_ALL, __io_async_cancel() calls io_try_cancel()
until nothing is found, and io_poll_cancel() cancels one request per
call, starting each lookup at the beginning of the hash. A cancelled
request stays hashed until its task work runs, so every lookup walks
past the ones already cancelled. Cancelling K of N pending polls visits
about K*N/2 requests in one io_uring_enter(), with uring_lock held.

A single CANCEL_FD|ALL on 80000 polls on one eventfd takes 17.06s,
0.02s with this change. With voluntary preemption the soft lockup
watchdog fires:

  watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#1 stuck for 26s! [repro:100]
  RIP: 0010:io_cancel_req_match+0x19/0xa0
   io_poll_cancel+0x73/0x170
   io_try_cancel+0x7b/0xf0
   __io_async_cancel+0x41/0x110

Walk the hash once and cancel every match, as io_cancel_remove() does
for futex and waitid. Cancel by user_data only needs its own bucket.
__io_async_cancel() still loops until nothing is found, so a request
that io-wq parks in the poll hash meanwhile is still cancelled.

A cancel that matches one request now walks the whole hash twice instead
of stopping at the match.

summary: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring: free the task context after a grace period

A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work()
running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or
io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else
branch:

    percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1);
    if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel)))
            wake_up(&tctx->wait);
    put_task_struct(tctx->task);

The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(),
and on exec it frees the tctx right after. Nothing holds that off for
the remaining three lines, the task reference only covers a tctx freed
along with the task_struct. It used to work out because
io_uring_del_tctx_node() took the uring_lock that the freeing side holds
across io_put_task(), until that moved to tctx_lock.

Free the tctx with kfree_rcu(), and enter an RCU read section in
io_put_task() before the count is dropped.

summary: io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/bpf-ops: clear bpf_ctx while submitting SQEs

bpf_io_uring_submit_sqes() calls io_submit_sqes() from inside the loop
program, with current->bpf_ctx set, and requests issued inline run with
it set too. The socket code uses has_current_bpf_ctx() to recognize
calls from bpf_setsockopt() and friends, where the caller holds the
socket lock and has already been vetted, and skips both.

So a SOCKET_URING_OP_SETSOCKOPT from the SQ passes sockopt_capable()
without the capability, and runs without lock_sock(). A task with no
capability can set SO_MARK, IP_TRANSPARENT or TCP_REPAIR, and two
threads changing IP_OPTIONS on one socket, one through the ring, double
free in no time. SOCK_DESTROY via IORING_OP_SENDMSG ends up in
tcp_abort() without the lock the same way.

Clear the run context around io_submit_sqes(). The SQEs come from
userspace and must be issued like those of any other ring. They still
run inside the program's RCU tasks trace read section, so a request
that sleeps there holds up that grace period, but other request types
do that already.

summary: io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/net: mask socket type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK in io_socket_bpf_populate()

When an IORING_OP_SOCKET request is prepared in io_socket_prep(),
sock->type retains creation flags such as SOCK_CLOEXEC and SOCK_NONBLOCK
until __sys_socket_file() masks them off with SOCK_TYPE_MASK during
execution.

However, io_socket_bpf_populate() copies sock->type into
bctx->socket.type without masking off ~SOCK_TYPE_MASK. As a result, a
cBPF filter inspecting bctx->socket.type against socket types such as
SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM can be bypassed by ORing SOCK_CLOEXEC or
SOCK_NONBLOCK into the socket type.

Mask sock->type with SOCK_TYPE_MASK when populating bctx->socket.type.

summary: io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

io_uring/register: enforce per-task restrictions in io_uring_register_blind()

When io_uring_register(2) is invoked with fd == -1, it dispatches
directly to io_uring_register_blind() without checking
current->io_uring_restrict.

As a result, a task with per-task register restrictions installed via
IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS can still invoke blind registration opcodes
such as IORING_REGISTER_SEND_MSG_RING even when those opcodes are not in
the task's allowed register_op bitmap.

Check current->io_uring_restrict->register_op in
io_uring_register_blind() before dispatching blind registration opcodes.

summary: perf/core: Fix group leader use-after-free after sibling detach
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

perf/core: Fix group leader use-after-free after sibling detach

perf_group_detach() handles leader and sibling detach differently. When the
group leader is detached, all siblings are promoted to singleton events and
their group_leader pointer is reset to themselves. When a sibling is
detached, it is removed from the leader's sibling_list, but its
group_leader pointer is left pointing at the old leader.

That is harmless when the sibling is being closed and freed immediately, as
in the DETACH_DEAD path. It is not safe when the sibling is detached but
kept alive, such as during CPU hotplug with DETACH_GROUP. In that case the
sibling is removed from the context, while its file descriptor can still
keep it alive.

A typical failing sequence is:

  - A group contains leader L and sibling S.
  - CPU hot-unplug detaches S with DETACH_GROUP, removing it from
    L->sibling_list but leaving S->group_leader == L.
  - L is later closed and freed.
  - A PERF_IOC_FLAG_GROUP ioctl on S follows S->group_leader and
    dereferences the freed leader.

This was reproduced by running the perf event fuzzer, CPU hotplug, and a
stress workload concurrently:

  Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address 006b6b6b6b6b6cdb
  CPU: 2 PID: 12489 Comm: perf_fuzzer 6.18.7 PREEMPT
  pc : perf_ioctl+0x34c/0xc68
  x20: ffffff89a3fa2c70 x8 : 6b6b6b6b6b6b6b6b
  Code: 943c4a0e 340047a0 f9404a94 f9411e88 (f940b908)
  Call trace:
  perf_ioctl+0x34c/0xc68 (P)
  __arm64_sys_ioctl+0xa0/0xf4
  invoke_syscall+0x58/0xe4
  el0_svc_common+0xa8/0xdc
  do_el0_svc+0x1c/0x28
  el0_svc+0x40/0xc0
  el0t_64_sync_handler+0x68/0xdc
  el0t_64_sync+0x1c4/0x1c8

The fault happened in perf_ioctl(), where perf_event_for_each() follows
the stale group_leader pointer and perf_event_for_each_child() then
dereferences the freed leader's context.

Fix the use-after-free by promoting the detached sibling to a singleton.
Also fix __event_disable() cgroup accounting and event state change.

summary: cipso: adjust cached option offsets when removing CIPSO
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cipso: adjust cached option offsets when removing CIPSO

cipso_v4_skbuff_delattr() removes the CIPSO bytes but does not adjust
cached offsets for options that follow them.

For example, with a valid 10-byte CIPSO option followed by a seven-byte
RR option, parsing records rr at offset 30.  Removing CIPSO moves RR to
offset 20, while the cached offset remains 30.  Consumers such as
ip_forward_options() and __ip_options_echo() then access the wrong bytes;
the latter may interpret packet data as the option length and copy it into
fixed-size option storage.

Mirror cipso_v4_delopt() and subtract cipso_len from the srr, rr, ts and
router_alert offsets when they follow CIPSO.  cipso_len is the distance
the first memmove() shifts those options.  The later header move and
network-header reset relocate the bytes and their offset base together.

summary: nvdimm/btt: reject an arena whose nfree is below the lane count
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvdimm/btt: reject an arena whose nfree is below the lane count

The BTT info block's nfree field, the number of reserve free blocks, is
read from the medium without validation.  btt_freelist_init() and
btt_rtt_init() size the per-lane freelist[] and rtt[] arrays by nfree,
but the I/O path indexes them by the lane from nd_region_acquire_lane(),
which is bounded by nd_region->num_lanes (ND_MAX_LANES), not by nfree.
A crafted or foreign arena whose nfree is below the lane count makes
freelist[lane]/rtt[lane] run past the allocation: an out-of-bounds write.

btt.rst documents the nlanes = min(nfree, num_cpus) invariant, which the
code does not currently honor: num_lanes is ND_MAX_LANES regardless of
nfree.  Reject an arena whose nfree is below num_lanes at discovery,
before the per-lane arrays are allocated, enforcing that invariant.

summary: scsi: qla2xxx: Unlink NVMe unsol ctx before freeing on LS reject error
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: qla2xxx: Unlink NVMe unsol ctx before freeing on LS reject error

qla_nvme_xmt_ls_rsp() obtains uctx, which was linked into
fcport->unsol_ctx_head by qla2xxx_process_purls_iocb() and is still linked
when the NVMe transport calls back to transmit the LS response. On the
error (out:) path the function frees uctx with kfree() but never removes
it from the list. This leaves a freed node in fcport->unsol_ctx_head: the
next list_add_tail() for that fcport writes through the freed node, and a
subsequent list_del() can corrupt the list or panic.

Unlink uctx with list_del() before kfree() on the error path, matching the
other free sites in qla_nvme_release_lsrsp_cmd_kref() and
qla2xxx_process_purls_pkt(). qla2x00_rel_sp() in the failure path only
returns the SRB to its pool and does not invoke sp->put_fn, so the out:
path is the sole free and uctx is always still linked there.

summary: slip: remove slip_hangup() to fix use-after-free in slip_receive_buf()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

slip: remove slip_hangup() to fix use-after-free in slip_receive_buf()

Jaeyoung Chung and Eulgyu Kim reported a slab-use-after-free read
in slip_receive_buf() when racing against tty hangup.

tty_ldisc_hangup() calls ld->ops->hangup() while holding only
a read lock on tty->ldisc_sem (via tty_ldisc_ref()).
Because slip_hangup() simply called slip_close(), it ran concurrently
with reader functions such as slip_receive_buf().

slip_close() unregisters and frees the net device and its private
struct slip, causing concurrent reader threads in slip_receive_buf()
to dereference freed memory.

Line discipline close() is already guaranteed to be called under
the write lock of tty->ldisc_sem during hangup processing
(in tty_ldisc_reinit() or tty_ldisc_kill()).

Remove slip_hangup() so teardown is serialized cleanly by slip_close().

summary: net/smc: fix socket use-after-free during link group termination
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/smc: fix socket use-after-free during link group termination

__smc_lgr_terminate() drops conns_lock after finding a connection in
lgr->conns_all, but before taking a reference on its socket. The connection
is embedded in the socket, and its registration reference protects it only
while the connection remains in the tree.

A concurrent close can unregister the connection and drop that reference,
freeing the socket before the termination worker reaches sock_hold().

The race is reachable when close overlaps link group termination.
Local stress testing reproduced the use-after-free and KASAN reported:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __smc_lgr_terminate.part.0 [smc]
  Write of size 4 by task kworker/3:3
  Workqueue: events smc_lgr_terminate_work [smc]
  __smc_lgr_terminate.part.0 [smc]

The socket was allocated by smc_create(), freed through
slab_free_after_rcu_debug(), and was followed by:

  refcount_t: addition on 0; use-after-free.
  __smc_lgr_terminate.part.0 [smc]

Take the socket reference while conns_lock still protects the tree entry.
The unregister path then cannot drop the last reference until termination
has finished using the socket.

summary: net: smc: fix splice entry lifetime imbalance in smc_rx_splice
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: smc: fix splice entry lifetime imbalance in smc_rx_splice

smc_rx_splice() passes pages to splice_to_pipe() before taking the
references that cover the lifetime of each splice entry. In the
VM-backed RMB path, splice_to_pipe() may drop unqueued entries through
smc_rx_spd_release(), while queued entries are released later via the
pipe buffer callback.

The old post-splice accounting also derives the number of queued VM pages
from an offset mutated while building the descriptor, and a multi-page
splice pairs one sock_hold() with multiple sock_put() calls.

Take the page and socket references for every candidate entry before
splice_to_pipe(), and drop the matching private state, page reference,
and socket reference from smc_rx_spd_release() for entries that never
get queued. This fixes a refcount imbalance that can underflow page
refcounts and trigger a use-after-free.

summary: wifi: mwifiex: use the subframe length when parsing A-MSDU TDLS frames
RDMA/siw: Bound fragmented header copies by the remaining length
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

RDMA/siw: Bound fragmented header copies by the remaining length

siw_get_hdr() can receive an extended DDP/RDMAP header across more than
one TCP callback. The first callback may receive most of the header,
while the next one still limits the copy to hdrlen - MIN_DDP_HDR instead
of the number of missing bytes. This makes the destination move past the
end of the header and overwrite the receive state, including
fpdu_part_rcvd. A later callback can then use a negative fpdu_part_rcvd
value as a copy offset, which creates an OOB write.

Use the number of header bytes already received when calculating the
next copy length.

summary: Bluetooth: bpa10x: avoid OOB read of revision string in bpa10x_setup()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

Bluetooth: bpa10x: avoid OOB read of revision string in bpa10x_setup()

bpa10x_setup() sends the vendor command 0xfc0e and passes the response
to bt_dev_info() and hci_set_fw_info() as a "%s" string starting at
skb->data + 1, without checking the length:

	bt_dev_info(hdev, "%s", (char *)(skb->data + 1));
	hci_set_fw_info(hdev, "%s", skb->data + 1);

A device that returns a one-byte response (status only) leaves
skb->data + 1 past the end of the data, and the %s walk reads adjacent
slab memory until it meets a NUL. The same happens when the payload is
not NUL-terminated within skb->len. The out-of-bounds bytes end up in
the kernel log and the firmware-info debugfs file.

Print the revision string with a bounded "%.*s" limited to skb->len - 1
instead. This keeps the string readable for well-behaved devices while
never reading past the received data, and does not fail setup, so a
device returning a short or unterminated response keeps working.

summary: wifi: mac80211: validate extension-frame layout before RX
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: validate extension-frame layout before RX

Extension frames only have the extension header at the regular 802.11
header offset. The generic RX path can still reach helpers and interface
dispatch code that read regular header address fields before unsupported
extension subtypes are dropped.

mac80211 currently only handles S1G beacon extension frames. Drop other
extension subtypes before they can reach regular-header RX processing.
For S1G beacons, linearize the SKB with the management-frame path and
require the fixed S1G beacon header, including optional fixed fields
indicated by frame control, before generic RX dispatch.

Route S1G beacons through the station/default-link RX path without
regular-header station lookup. Avoid regular-header address reads in the
mac80211 RX paths that process S1G extension beacons, including
accept-frame, duplicate-detection, address-copy, and MLO
address-translation paths.

Also make ieee80211_get_bssid() length-safe before returning the S1G
source-address pointer.

summary: wifi: mwifiex: bound uAP association event IEs to the event buffer
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mwifiex: bound uAP association event IEs to the event buffer

mwifiex_process_uap_event() handles EVENT_UAP_STA_ASSOC by exposing the
(re)association request IEs that the firmware copies into the event:

	sinfo->assoc_req_ies = &event->data[len];
	len = (u8 *)sinfo->assoc_req_ies - (u8 *)&event->frame_control;
	sinfo->assoc_req_ies_len = le16_to_cpu(event->len) - (u16)len;

event->len is supplied by the device firmware and is never validated,
and the subtraction is unchecked.  assoc_req_ies points into
adapter->event_body[MAX_EVENT_SIZE], a fixed-size array embedded in the
kmalloc()'d struct mwifiex_adapter.

On the ap_11n_enabled path mwifiex_set_sta_ht_cap() walks these IEs with
cfg80211_find_ie(), whose for_each_element() loop dereferences each
element header.  A firmware-reported event->len larger than the bytes
actually received makes assoc_req_ies_len describe IEs that extend past
event_body, so the walk reads out of the adapter slab object, a
slab-out-of-bounds read (KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in cfg80211_find_ie).
An event->len smaller than the header instead makes the int subtraction
negative, which wraps to a huge size_t when stored in assoc_req_ies_len.
The same length is handed to cfg80211_new_sta(), so a more modest
over-claim can also copy stale event_body bytes into the
NL80211_CMD_NEW_STATION notification.

A malicious or malfunctioning mwifiex device (USB/SDIO/PCIe) can deliver
such an event while the interface is in AP/uAP mode.

Validate event->len before use: reject a length that underflows the
header or that would place the IEs outside the event_body[] buffer the
event was copied into.  event->len here is struct mwifiex_assoc_event.len,
a payload field internal to this event, not the transport frame length,
so it is validated in this handler rather than at the generic
MWIFIEX_TYPE_EVENT receive path, which only sees the event cause and the
transport frame length.  The bound is against event_body[MAX_EVENT_SIZE]
rather than the actually-received length because the transports store the
event differently (USB and SDIO leave the 4-byte event header in
event_skb, PCIe strips it via skb_pull), whereas event_body is the single
fixed buffer all of them copy the event into.  This is the event-path
analogue of the receive-path bounds checks added in commit 119585281617
("wifi: mwifiex: Fix OOB and integer underflow when rx packets").

summary: proc: protect ptrace_may_access() with exec_update_lock (FD links)
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

proc: protect ptrace_may_access() with exec_update_lock (FD links)

proc_pid_get_link() and proc_pid_readlink() currently look up the task from
the pid once, then do the ptrace access check on that task, then look up
the task from the pid a second time to do the actual access.
That's racy in several ways.

To fix it, pass the task to the ->proc_get_link() handler, and instead of
proc_fd_access_allowed(), introduce a new helper call_proc_get_link() that
looks up and locks the task, does the access check, and calls
->proc_get_link().

summary: wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

wifi: mac80211: reinstate IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg()

The commit 592234e941f1 ("wifi: mac80211: Fix iTXQ AMPDU fragmentation
handling") changed the way handling of the IEEE80211_TX_CTL_AMPDU flag
is done in mac80211, so the only place it is set is in
ieee80211_tx_dequeue().

This means that any frames that are sent to the driver via drv_tx() will
no longer have the flag set. In particular, this affects packets going
through ieee80211_tx_pending(). Evan reported that this can result in
the ath9k driver failing to account such packets in its block ack
window, eventually overrunning the window and stalling TX.

Fix this by reinstating the flag in ieee80211_tx_prep_agg() when inside
a valid block ack window. This should be harmless for the TXQ path, and
will reinstate the previous behaviour for drivers that use the flag as a
signal to track the packet in the window.

summary: ALSA: emux: Fix UAF of soundfont zones at note-on
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: emux: Fix UAF of soundfont zones at note-on

snd_emux_note_on() looks up the matching zones via
snd_soundfont_search_zone(), which takes sflist->lock only during the
lookup and returns the raw zone pointers after releasing it.  The
caller then stores them in vp->zone without any protection.
Meanwhile, a concurrent SNDRV_EMUX_IOCTL_REMOVE_LAST_SAMPLES ioctl may
unlink and free those zones in snd_soundfont_remove_unlocked(); this
leads to a use-after-free in snd_emux_note_on(), and later at
accessing the cached vp->zone, e.g. in snd_emux_send_effect().

Fix it by holding sflist->lock in snd_emux_note_on() over the whole
zone lookup and voice setup, and let snd_soundfont_search_zone()
require the caller to hold the lock, instead.
snd_soundfont_lock_preset() takes sflist->lock for setting
presets_locked, so the removal path now syncs with the note-on finish.

summary: batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: stop originator purge worker before freeing TT

batadv_mesh_free() releases the translation tables via batadv_tt_free()
before batadv_originator_free() stops orig_work. The purge worker can
therefore still run while the TT is torn down. When an originator times
out, batadv_purge_orig_ref() calls batadv_tt_global_del_orig(), which
loads tt.global_hash and walks all buckets while taking their locks:

  CPU0                          CPU1
  batadv_tt_free()              batadv_purge_orig()
                                  batadv_tt_global_del_orig()
                                    hash = ...tt.global_hash;
    batadv_tt_global_table_free()
      batadv_hash_destroy(hash);
                                    spin_lock_bh(&hash->list_locks[i]);

Disable orig_work at the beginning of batadv_mesh_free(), directly after
the mesh was marked as deactivating. The second
disable_delayed_work_sync() in batadv_originator_free() is harmless because
it is free'd anyway.

summary: KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Cap number of parent PTEs per SP at 1000 (the arbitrary rmap limit)

When potentially reusing a shadow page, zap the shadow page if its number
of parent PTEs exceeds KVM's (mostly) arbitrary rmap recycling threshold.
Letting the guest create a (mostly) unbounded number of parent PTEs allows
the guest to coerce KVM into creating lists containing millions of PTEs,
effectively bounded only by the maximum number of shadow pages.

Because PTE lists are simple singly linked lists, removal is O(n).  Even
worse, if a list is constructed just so, teardown can be O(n^2), e.g. if
SPTEs are built such that zapping child SPTEs always zaps the last entry
in the list.  To cap things off, all paths that walk PTE lists do so
while holding mmu_lock, without conditionally rescheduling.

Using a doubly linked list would not address the issue, as removal would
remain O(n) since KVM still wouldn't know where in the list to remove from.
Removal could be made O(1) by storing a per-SPTE pointer, but that would
largely defeat the purpose of reusing SPs, and would penalize well-behaved
guests, especially for nested TDP where aliasing page tables is uncommon.

So, cap the maximum number of parent PTEs at the rmap limit.  In practice,
well-behaved guests will likely never run afoul of the limit.  E.g. when
running Linux as L1 with TDP, the number of parent PTEs for a single SP
tops out at under 200 (though undoubtedly obscure workloads can push it
higher).  Deliberately use a "greater than or equal" as opposed to rmap's
strictly "greater than", as the rmap code checks the threshold immediately
*after* inserting into the list, i.e. the limit is 1000 for rmaps, KVM just
very briefly blows past it.

Apply the check to both indirect and direct SPs, because while a fully
direct MMU naturally limits the number of parent PTEs to '1', direct SPs in
indirect MMUs have no such constraint.  E.g. if the guest maps a huge PTE
into many locations in its page tables, and KVM is backing the hugepage
with a direct SP, i.e. with a series of smaller pages, then KVM could end
up with a direct SP with many parents.

Note, shadow_mmu_try_split_huge_pages() always restarts the rmap walk or
bails entirely if it gets to the point where it tries to grab a SP, i.e.
there is *no* pre-existing bug that would be tripped by zapping a SP and
thus rmaps when getting a SP.

summary: smb: client: don't resurrect an exiting tcon from cached dir workers
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: don't resurrect an exiting tcon from cached dir workers

cfids_laundromat_worker() bumps tcon->tc_count for every expired open
cfid and queues cached_dir_offload_close() without checking whether the
tcon is already being torn down.  Racing with the final cifs_put_tcon(),
the tcon comes back from zero and gets torn down twice:

  T1                                  T2
  cifs_put_tcon()
   --tc_count == 0, TID_EXITING
   tconInfoFree()
    free_cached_dirs()
     cancel_delayed_work_sync()       cfids_laundromat_worker()
                                       ++tc_count == 1
                                       queue_work(serverclose_wq)
    kfree(tcon->origin_fullpath)
    kfree(tcon)
                                      cached_dir_offload_close()
                                       close_cached_dir()  [UAF]
                                       cifs_put_tcon()
                                        tconInfoFree()     [double free]

cached_dir_lease_break() also bumps tc_count without tc_lock, racing with
the laundromat's locked update.

Take the tcon reference through a helper that refuses once the tcon is
TID_EXITING or its refcount has dropped to zero.  Queued put_work and
close_work then always hold a tcon reference, so tconInfoFree() can't
run before they finish and free_cached_dirs() doesn't need to flush any
workqueue.  If the laundromat can't get a reference, put the cfid back on
the dying list for free_cached_dirs() to free; its handle goes away with
the tree connection.

The lease break path finds the tcon on ses->tcon_list under
cifs_tcp_ses_lock, so it can't see TID_EXITING, but it now takes tc_lock.

summary: mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: stop retrying folios that cannot be split

A fault or collapse can insert a large folio crossing EOF after
shmem_undo_range() has handled the boundary folios. If splitting that
folio fails, truncate_inode_partial_folio() retains it when it is dirty.
The final scan then repeatedly finds it because it restarts from an
unchanged start.

Truncation keeps the inode lock and ignores fatal signals while looping.
A concurrent unlink() can then block other directory operations while
holding the directory lock and waiting for the file's lock.

Advance start past the retained folio, whose truncated part has already
been zeroed. Do not move start backwards if the failed split has shrunk
the folio.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: split fixes, simplify descriptions, adjust comments ]

summary: ocfs2: cache the mount context for dentry lock callbacks
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: cache the mount context for dentry lock callbacks

ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock() drops the inode reference before releasing the
DENTRY lock.  This lets inode eviction release the local inode and open
locks before a remote unlink can proceed past the DENTRY lock.

A DLM callback can still arrive before the DENTRY lock has been dropped.
ocfs2_get_dentry_osb() obtains the mount context through dl_inode->i_sb,
which can access a freed inode when the downconvert thread drops the
last inode reference in its post-unlock callback:

  Downconvert thread                     DLM callback thread
  ------------------                     -------------------
  ocfs2_process_blocked_lock()
    ocfs2_dentry_post_unlock()
      ocfs2_dentry_lock_put()
        ocfs2_drop_dentry_lock()
          iput(dl->dl_inode)
          [inode reclaimed after RCU]
                                         ocfs2_blocking_ast()
                                           ocfs2_get_dentry_osb()
                                             dl->dl_inode->i_sb
          ocfs2_simple_drop_lockres()

Store the mount context in the DENTRY lock resource's l_priv field and use
the default mount-context lookup.  Recover the containing dentry lock with
container_of(), as already done for refcount locks, and remove
ocfs2_get_dentry_osb().  ocfs2_dismount_volume() shuts down the DLM before
freeing the mount context, so callbacks can use it without accessing the
inode.  Preserve the existing iput-before-unlock order to avoid delaying
local inode and open lock release until after the DENTRY lock is released.

summary: HID: wacom: Advertise SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability prior to registration
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: wacom: Advertise SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability prior to registration

Input subsystem guidelines require that device capabilities are advertised
before the input device is registered.  The Wacom driver was violating
this by advertising the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability post-registration in
wacom_set_shared_values() (and duplicating it in device-specific setup
cases).

Resolve this by moving the SW_MUTE_DEVICE capability setup to
wacom_setup_touch_input_capabilities() for all touch devices that support
it.

For generic touch devices whose capabilities depend on mute switch
usages parsed from a sibling Pen/Pad interface, defer registration
with -EPROBE_DEFER until the sibling has parsed its descriptors and
initialized shared capabilities.

summary: mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/cma: accept memory of multi-range CMA areas

Patch series "mm/cma: accept memory of CMA areas reserved with
memblock_reserve()", v1.

Pages of allocated CMA areas are released to the buddy allocator with
__free_pages(), which does not check for unaccepted memory.

This usually works because memblock accepts the memory it allocates.

However, multi-range CMA areas, used by hugetlb_cma, and fixed CMA areas
requested with cma=<size>@<base> are reserved with memblock_reserve() and
their memory is never accepted.

On TDX and SEV-SNP guests the first access to such a page is fatal.

To ease the backporting, each case is addressed by a separate patch:
- patch 1 accepts the memory of multi-range CMA areas
- patch 2 does the same for the fixed CMA areas

The second patch won't apply cleanly to 6.6 and 6.12, but I believe the
stable team LLMs will take care of that :)


This patch (of 2):

On systems with unaccepted memory, memblock allocations accept the
allocated range, but when cma_declare_contiguous_multi() uses open coded
allocation of multiple ranges, it reserves them with memblock_reserve()
and they are never accepted.

These pages are released to the buddy allocator by cma_activate_area()
with __free_pages() that does not check for unaccepted memory, so the
first access to such a page in a TDX or SEV-SNP guest is fatal.

Accept the memory of each range when it is reserved.

summary: drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/v3d: Widen cache_clean_lock over the whole L2TCACTL sequence

v3d_clean_caches() and v3d_flush_l2t() both write the single L2TCACTL
register and poll its status bits. The mutex cache_clean_lock exists to
serialize them, but v3d_clean_caches() only took the lock around its final
FLM_CLEAN write.

These functions run concurrently: v3d_flush_l2t() is issued from the
BIN/RENDER/CSD invalidate path while v3d_clean_caches() runs from the
CACHE_CLEAN queue, and each queue's scheduler uses its own ordered
workqueue, so their run_job callbacks execute in parallel.

Because clean locked only its final write, a concurrent flush can write
L2TCACTL during clean's unlocked phase. Both use non read-modify-write
writes to the one register, so whichever lands last wins: clean's TMUWCF
write can land on the flush's in-flight L2TFLS invalidate, triggering the
GFXH-1897 hazard of writing L2TCACTL while a flush is pending.

Hold cache_clean_lock across the entire L2TCACTL access sequence so it
is fully mutually exclusive with v3d_flush_l2t(), which already takes the
lock around its own write.

summary: mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb: fix mremap deadlock when PMD sharing is possible

move_hugetlb_page_tables() holds the mapping's i_mmap_rwsem for
write while moving hugetlb PTEs. This prevents races with truncation
and protects huge_pmd_unshare(), but the move loop must not call
helpers that can acquire the same rwsem for read.

huge_pte_alloc() can do that when the destination can use PMD
sharing: it may call huge_pmd_share(), which takes i_mmap_rwsem for
read while searching for a shareable PMD table. Calling it while the
move path already holds i_mmap_rwsem for write can deadlock.

Avoid that path for PMD-sized hugetlb mappings that can use PMD
sharing. Instead of allocating or sharing the destination page table
while moving, zap the source range and let the destination fault path
populate or share the PMD lazily.

Reuse the hugetlb unmap logic for the source-side zap by splitting
the core loop out of __unmap_hugepage_range(). The wrapper keeps the
existing tlb_start_vma(), tlb_end_vma() and huge_pmd_unshare_flush()
behavior, while move_hugetlb_page_tables() can reuse the unmap loop
with its existing mmu_gather.

summary: smb: client: fix OOB read of the resume name sent in TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix OOB read of the resume name sent in TRANS2_FIND_NEXT2

cifs_fill_dirent() reads the fixed part of a directory entry and the
name length it holds, or for SMB_FIND_FILE_UNIX scans the name for its
terminating NUL, without knowing where the response ends.
cifs_save_resume_key() calls it for the entry at the LastNameOffset the
server chose, after every FindNext and after the FindFirst of a search
rewind, and records the name it returns as the resume name of the
search without bounding it; the next CIFSFindNext() copies up to
PATH_MAX - 1 bytes from that name into its request and sends them to
the server. cifs_filldir() bounds
the name against the end of the response since
commit f8cf09a53a0d ("smb: client: bound dirent name against end of
SMB response in cifs_filldir"), but only after cifs_fill_dirent() has
read the entry, and nxt_dir_entry() checks the entries it walks only
against sizeof(FILE_DIRECTORY_INFO), for every level but
SMB_FIND_FILE_INFO_STANDARD, and never sees the first entry of a
response.

Bounding where last_entry starts, as the preceding patch does, does
not bound the read. A last entry that starts within the final bytes of

summary: lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

lockd: Fix use-after-free in nlmsvc_retry_blocked

nlmsvc_retry_blocked() examines the block at the head of nlm_blocked
under nlm_blocked_lock, then releases the lock before calling
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() or retry_deferred_block(). The nlm_blocked list
reference is all that keeps the block alive across that window.
nlmsvc_grant_blocked() does take one of its own, but not until after
the lock has been dropped. Unmounting the nfsd filesystem while a lock
request is still blocked reaches nlmsvc_traverse_blocks(), which drops
the list reference and frees the block along with the nlm_rqst hanging
off it.

summary: ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: serialize migration MLE cleanup on failure

A migration MLE has a base reference for the mastering answer and an
in-use reference held by dlm_migrate_lockres(). The finishing assertion
consumes the base reference, but migration failure drops it again
without checking whether the assertion already consumed it.

The target queues its migration worker before it acknowledges the
ALL_DONE packet, so its finishing assertion can be handled while the
sender still waits for the status. If the connection fails before the
status arrives, dlm_send_one_lockres() returns an error for a migration
that the target has already completed:

  Old-master sender                  Finishing assertion
  -----------------                  -------------------
  publish MLE; take in-use reference
  send ALL_DONE; wait for status
                                     take lookup reference
                                     unlink MLE
                                     put lookup and base references
  send returns a connection error
  put base reference again; free MLE
  put in-use reference; access freed MLE

dlm_assert_master_handler() holds dlm->spinlock from the MLE lookup to
the final puts, and it takes dlm->master_lock around the unlink and the
puts. Decide under the same locks: if the MLE is already unhashed, the
assertion consumed the base reference, so drop only the sender's in-use
reference. Otherwise unlink it before consuming the base reference so a
later assertion no longer finds it.

An assertion that got there first has also made the target the owner
and cleared DLM_LOCK_RES_MIGRATING. Treating the attempt as failed at
that point would leave the lockres owned by the target while this node
still holds the other nodes' locks and refmap bits, so it could neither
be purged nor migrated again. Finish our side as a completed migration
does instead: drop those locks under res->spinlock if the target still
owns the lockres, and recalculate its usage.

Use the same cleanup for the pre-send failure, the send failure and the
target-death failure paths. The sender's in-use reference keeps the MLE
alive until its final put outside the nested locks. Successful
migration retains its existing in-use-only put.

A target that has died cannot assert after the sender has seen its
death. The o2net node-down callback runs before the DLM one; it
disconnects the node and flushes the workqueue that runs the message
handlers, so an assertion already received has been handled by the time
the DLM removes the node from the domain map. A node that leaves the
domain cleanly sends its exit message only after its assertions have
been answered.

Two windows of the hand-over itself are left as they are: the handler
switches the owner and the sender drops the other nodes' locks moments
later, and an assertion from a live target that arrives after the
sender has given up still meets the owner check in the handler. Waiting
for the target before giving up would only stretch the first window
into the time in which recovery of the target can observe it.

summary: nvme: Do not drop the cdev reference twice when cdev_device_add() fails
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme: Do not drop the cdev reference twice when cdev_device_add() fails

Since commit 9952f3882ecb ("nvme: fix cdev lifetime"),
nvme_add_ns_cdev() and nvme_add_ns_head_cdev() take a reference to the
namespace (or namespace head) before calling nvme_cdev_add(), to be
dropped by the char device's release, nvme_cdev_rel(), and drop it
themselves when nvme_cdev_add() fails. But when cdev_device_add()
fails, nvme_cdev_add() has already put the device, and nvme_cdev_rel()
has already dropped that reference: the caller drops it a second time.

With one allocation failure injected into cdev_device_add() for a
namespace on an NVMe over loop controller, deleting the controller
gives, with native multipath:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in nvme_put_ns_head+0x21/0x140
  Write of size 4 at addr ff1100000a4ea078 by task init/1
   nvme_put_ns_head
   nvme_put_ns
   nvme_remove_namespaces
   nvme_do_delete_ctrl
   nvme_delete_ctrl_sync
   nvme_sysfs_delete
  Freed by task 1:
   kfree
   nvme_ns_remove
   nvme_remove_namespaces
  refcount_t: underflow; use-after-free.

Take the reference in nvme_cdev_add() instead, right before
cdev_device_add(), and let the callers neither take nor drop it. Add
nvme_is_ns_cdev() for the check that nvme_cdev_rel() and nvme_cdev_add()
now share.

summary: drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and erase
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and erase

panthor_group_destroy() checks the GROUP_REGISTERED mark and then calls
xa_erase() without holding the xarray lock across both. If the handle is
destroyed by another thread in between, and a concurrent GROUP_CREATE
reuses the freed ID, the first destroy erases and releases the new,
still-initializing group, leading to a use-after-free in
panthor_group_create().

Do the mark check and erase atomically under xa_lock().

summary: scsi: aic79xx: Fix NULL pointer dereference in device reset
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: aic79xx: Fix NULL pointer dereference in device reset

Since commit c67e63800446 ("scsi: aic79xx: Do not reference SCSI command
when resetting device") the device reset SCB has no SCSI command, but
ahd_linux_dev_reset() still sets its residual, and ahd_abort_scbs(), which
completes it, sets its status. Seen on an AIC-7902 when a failing disk
triggered a device reset, which killed the SCSI error handler:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000009c
  EIP: ahd_linux_dev_reset.cold+0xee/0x26e

Add NULL command checks to the accessors in aic79xx_osm.h. Also skip
autosense for an SCB without a command and complete it with ahd_done()
right away: the REQUEST SENSE path can clear SCB_DEVICE_RESET, after which
ahd_done() would dereference the missing command.

summary: accel/amdxdna: clear the mailbox channel pointer when starting it fails
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

accel/amdxdna: clear the mailbox channel pointer when starting it fails

aie2_create_context() allocates a mailbox channel, starts it, and on a
failed start frees it again:

	hwctx->priv->mbox_chann = xdna_mailbox_alloc_channel(ndev->mbox);
	...
	ret = xdna_mailbox_start_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann, ...);
	if (ret)
		goto free_channel;
	...
free_channel:
	xdna_mailbox_free_channel(hwctx->priv->mbox_chann);

hwctx->priv->mbox_chann keeps pointing at the freed channel. That
pointer is the driver's own test for whether a hardware context has a
usable channel: aie2_destroy_context() returns early on NULL,
aie2_sched_job_run() refuses to run a job on NULL, and the message
helpers return -ENODEV on NULL. A stale pointer passes all of them.

It matters on the restart path. aie2_hwctx_restart() calls
aie2_create_context() again on a hardware context that is already live,
after aie2_hwctx_stop() has torn its channel down, and the context
survives a failure there: aie2_sched_job_timedout() discards the return
value entirely, and aie2_hwctx_resume() only propagates it. What is
left is a live hardware context holding a freed channel, and every
later user of it takes the non-NULL branch:

  - the next job submitted reaches xdna_mailbox_send_msg() on the freed
    channel, via the !mbox_chann guard in aie2_sched_job_run(),
  - a second command timeout reaches aie2_hwctx_stop() ->
    aie2_destroy_context(),
  - closing the device reaches aie2_hwctx_fini() ->
    aie2_release_resource() -> xrs_release_resource() ->
    aie2_xrs_unload() -> aie2_destroy_context(),

and aie2_destroy_context() then calls xdna_mailbox_stop_channel()
followed by xdna_mailbox_free_channel() on memory that was already
freed: a use-after-free, and a second free of the same channel.

The AIE4 management channel already does this correctly -
aie4_mailbox_start() clears ndev->aie.mgmt_chann right after freeing
it. Do the same here.

The create path itself is not affected: when aie2_xrs_load() fails,
xrs_allocate_resource() removes the solver node without calling
->unload, and aie2_hwctx_init() frees hwctx->priv, so the stale pointer
never outlives the structure holding it.

Starting a channel can fail today without this patch: the ring buffer
sizes firmware reports are rejected unless both are powers of two, and
request_irq() can fail.

summary: ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header

When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by
the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then
authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names.
Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than
one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's
key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt
from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session
identity, and it is checked against the wrong session.

MS-SMB2 says the server must check that the transform SessionId
matches the one in the decrypted SMB2 header and treat a mismatch
as a protocol error. Add that check in __handle_ksmbd_work() after
decryption, before dispatching: the message has to be at least one
fixed SMB2 header, the first operation must not set
SMB2_FLAGS_RELATED_OPERATIONS and its SessionId must match the
transform SessionId, and every following non-related operation in
a compound chain must carry the same SessionId. NextCommand
offsets must be 8-byte aligned and stay inside the message; the
bounds check is done by subtraction so it cannot wrap.

When the decrypted payload is a compression transform, the
existing decompression step runs first and the decompressed SMB2
message is checked instead, since a compression transform header
carries no SessionId.

summary: xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: fix temporary cursor leak in btree shift corruption paths

In xfs_btree_lshift and xfs_btree_rshift, when XFS_IS_CORRUPT detects
an invalid firstrec/lastrec result after xfs_btree_dup_cursor has
successfully allocated a temporary cursor, the error path jumps to
error0 which returns without freeing tcur.  This leaks the cursor
memory, the xfs_group reference, and the per-level buffer references
held by the duplicated cursor.  Jump to error1 instead, which calls
xfs_btree_del_cursor(tcur, XFS_BTREE_ERROR) to properly release all
resources.

summary: s390/zcrypt: Fix out-of-bounds ptr advance in cca_query_crypto_facility()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/zcrypt: Fix out-of-bounds ptr advance in cca_query_crypto_facility()

The FQ reply parser code blindly advanced the walk pointer by a length
value read directly from the hardware reply payload without checking
that the advance stayed within the allocated reply buffer. A corrupt
or malicious device response could push ptr beyond the cprbmem region,
causing an out-of-bounds dereference or kernel memory exposure via the
subsequent memcpy().

Fix this by tracking the remaining reply buffer space in a variable
and validating each device-supplied length field against it before
advancing or dereferencing the pointer.

summary: KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refresh
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: pfncache: use a dedicated invalidation sequence for cache refresh

The gfn_to_pfn_cache refresh path guards against mmu notifier
invalidations which complete while it has dropped gpc->lock for the
HVA->PFN lookup: hva_to_pfn_retry() samples kvm->mmu_invalidate_seq
and retries if it changed, or if mn_active_invalidate_count is still
elevated.

That is insufficient for HVA-based caches. mmu_invalidate_seq is only
advanced by kvm_mmu_invalidate_end() when the invalidated range
overlaps a memslot, and an HVA-based cache (e.g. the Xen shared_info
page mapped with KVM_XEN_ATTR_TYPE_SHARED_INFO_HVA) need not be backed
by any memslot at all. An invalidation of the cached HVA which starts
and ends entirely within the lookup window is thus invisible to the
retry check: mn_active_invalidate_count is back to zero and the
sequence never moved. The refresh then publishes a mapping of a page
which has already been freed, and the next reader dereferences it:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in kvm_xen_shared_info_init+0x3c6/0x440
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff8880599c2900 by task syz.2.383/7257

Since gfn_to_pfn_cache_invalidate_start() deliberately skips caches
which are not currently valid (including one whose refresh is in
progress, as the refresh clears the valid flag before dropping the
lock), the retry check is the only line of defence, and it must fire
for *any* invalidation, not just those hitting a memslot.

Add a dedicated kvm->gpc_invalidate_seq, incremented by every
kvm_mmu_notifier_invalidate_range_end() under mn_invalidate_lock
before mn_active_invalidate_count is decremented, and check it in
hva_to_pfn_retry() instead of mmu_invalidate_seq. Incrementing in
range_end() in the same critical section as the in-progress count
also closes the variant where the cache is activated with the
contested HVA only after invalidate_range_start() has run.

The same bug is also reachable through the per-vCPU vcpu_info cache
(KVM_XEN_VCPU_ATTR_TYPE_VCPU_INFO_HVA), where the stale mapping is
then dereferenced by kvm_setup_guest_pvclock() on the next KVM_RUN:

  BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in kvm_setup_guest_pvclock+0x5bf/0x660

This intentionally makes refresh retry on *unrelated* mmu notifier
events; restoring precision (and reworking the GPC locking more
generally) is left for a subsequent series.

Reproducers: https://david.woodhou.se/xen_shinfo_race.c
             https://david.woodhou.se/vcpu_info_race.c

summary: net/9p/usbg: remove bogus context initialization in alloc_requests
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: remove bogus context initialization in alloc_requests

alloc_requests() initializes usb9pfs->in_req->context to point at the
struct f_usb9pfs instance itself. usb9pfs_queue_tx() later overwrites
this with the real struct p9_req_t pointer before every transmit, and
usb9pfs_tx_complete() clears it back to NULL after each completion, so
in_req->context only ever holds a valid p9_req_t once a request has
actually been queued.

usb9pfs_clear_tx(), however, can run at any time (mount close, gadget
disable) independent of whether a request was ever queued. If it runs
before the first usb9pfs_transmit(), it reads the leftover sentinel
value, type-confuses the struct f_usb9pfs pointer as a struct
p9_req_t, and both writes through it (req->t_err = -ECONNRESET) and
hands it to p9_client_cb(), which manipulates req->wq and req->refcount
at bogus offsets inside f_usb9pfs. This reliably corrupts memory or
panics whenever the transport is torn down before any 9p request has
been transmitted, e.g. mounting and immediately unmounting, or a cable
disconnect racing the very first request.

usb9pfs->out_req->context is set the same way but is never read by
this transport (usb9pfs_rx_complete() identifies the instance via
ep->driver_data instead), so it serves no purpose either.

Both endpoints' ->driver_data are already set to usb9pfs in
enable_endpoint(), which is what the completion handlers actually use
to recover the f_usb9pfs instance. Just drop the leftover
->context assignments; usb_ep_alloc_request()/alloc_ep_req() already
return zeroed requests, so in_req->context correctly starts out NULL.

summary: rust: configfs: fix data offset calculation for subsystem callbacks
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust: configfs: fix data offset calculation for subsystem callbacks

`get_group_data()` chooses between `Group::<Parent>::container_of()` and
`Subsystem::<Parent>::container_of()` based on whether `this` represents
the root group of a configfs subsystem. It detects this by checking
`(*this).cg_subsys.is_null()`, but `link_group()` in `fs/configfs/dir.c`
unconditionally sets `cg_subsys` for every `config_group` attached anywhere
in a registered subsystem, including the subsystem's own `su_group`. The
only `config_group` with a NULL `cg_subsys` is the configfs root, on which
userspace cannot trigger callbacks. The check is therefore always false at
runtime, and the `Subsystem` branch is dead. Subsystem-level callbacks
reach the `Group` branch and may read `data` at the wrong offset.

Thus change the `is_root` check to correctly identify whether a group is a
root group by comparing `this` to `subsys.su_group`.

summary: mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: memcontrol: fix NULL pointer deref and UAF from high_work_func() on dying memcg

When memory.high is exceeded in non-task context, try_charge_memcg()
schedules memcg->high_work without taking a reference on the memcg, and
high_work_func() invokes reclaim_high() without pinning the memcg.

With obj_cgroup reparenting, introduced in commit bf4f059954dc ("mm:
memcg/slab: obj_cgroup API"), objects charged to a child memcg are
reparented to its parent in mem_cgroup_css_offline() instead of holding a
reference on the child until uncharged.  Subsequent uncharges of those
objects go to the parent, which can leave the child's memory use
permanently above its high limit, so any later charge on the offlined
memcg in non-task context schedules high_work.  This was later widened
from kernel memory to LRU folios when commit f1cf8d2f36dc ("mm:
memcontrol: eliminate the problem of dying memory cgroup for LRU folios")
converted LRU folios to use obj_cgroup reparenting.

cancel_work_sync(&memcg->high_work) only runs at the end of teardown in
mem_cgroup_css_free(), so high_work_func() can start or still be running
reclaim_high() after mem_cgroup_css_released() or shrink_many() has called
lru_gen_release_memcg() and unhashed lruvec->lrugen.list.  If reclaim
tries to rotate the memcg, lru_gen_rotate_memcg() dereferences a NULL
pprev pointer.  This issue is specific to MGLRU and was introduced with
the memcg LRU in commit e4dde56cd208 ("mm: multi-gen LRU: per-node
lru_gen_folio lists").

With either traditional LRU or MGLRU, css_free_rwork_fn() calls
css_rstat_exit() which frees per-CPU rstat data before calling
mem_cgroup_css_free().  If reclaim_high() is still running, rstat updates
via mod_lruvec_state() -> __css_rstat_updated() cause a use-after-free on
the per-CPU rstat data.  This was introduced when commit 5da3bfa029d6
("cgroup: use separate rstat trees for each subsystem") moved
css_rstat_exit() ahead of ss->css_free().

Fix both problems by acquiring a reference with css_tryget_online() in
high_work_func() before calling reclaim_high(), and by resetting
memory.high and swap.high to PAGE_COUNTER_MAX in mem_cgroup_css_offline()
so that charges via references on an offlined memcg do not trigger
high_work on the dead child and skip checking live ancestors in
try_charge_memcg().

Acquiring the reference in high_work_func() rather than before scheduling
high_work is safe because mem_cgroup_css_free() calls irq_work_sync() and
cancel_work_sync() which cancels pending work and waits for an already
running high_work_func() to complete before mem_cgroup_free() frees the
memcg.  css_tryget_online() uses percpu_ref_tryget_live() and is safe to
call after percpu_ref_exit() before the cgroup is freed unlike
css_tryget().
