summary: mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/page-writeback: avoid 32-bit overflow in dirty threshold shares

The ratios used by __wb_calc_thresh() are scaled to parts per million, but
the threshold and ratio operands are unsigned long.  On 32-bit kernels,
their multiplication can wrap before the result is assigned to u64.

For example, with a threshold of 25600 pages and the default maximum ratio
of 1000000, wb_max_thresh becomes 4125 pages instead of 25600.  The shared
threshold and minimum share calculations can overflow in the same way,
producing incorrect per-writeback dirty limits.

Use a u64 threshold for the three ratio multiplications and div_u64() to
retain the existing division order and rounding.

summary: mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: fix truncate hang in large swap entry

Truncating a tmpfs file or memfd to a page-aligned size inside a large
swap entry can loop indefinitely in shmem_undo_range(). The task holds
the inode lock and cannot be killed.

A large swap entry represents a whole swapped-out folio. For example,
truncate a file whose pages 0-7 share one swap entry to four pages:

    [ 0  1  2  3 | 4  5  6  7 ]
         keep    |   discard
                 ^
            new EOF, start = 4

i_size has already been updated when boundary handling asks
shmem_get_partial_folio() for page 4. Since it is swapped out, the helper
calls shmem_get_folio() with SGP_READ. That rejects page 4 with -EINVAL
because its starting offset equals i_size. Nothing is read back.

The final scan cannot free the entry without losing pages 0-3. It skips
it, restarts from start = 4, and finds it again indefinitely. An unaligned
truncate avoids this particular failure because the requested page starts
below i_size. Folios already in the page-cache cannot trigger it as the
direct lookup will return them beyond EOF.

Fix it by letting shmem_get_partial_folio() call shmem_swapin_folio()
directly for swap entries. This bypasses the read path's i_size check,
allowing the existing boundary handling to zero and split the folio. If
swap-in returns a smaller folio, it also splits the swap entry so the
final scan can free the entries beyond EOF. Retry the lookup if the entry
changes during swap-in.

Handling swap-in allocation failures remains broken and is unchanged by
this commit. Even when shmem_swapin_folio() correctly returns -ENOMEM
instead of -EEXIST, shmem_get_partial_folio() returns NULL and
shmem_undo_range() skips boundary handling. If the large swap entry
remains intact, truncation can still loop in the final scan, while hole
punching can return without zeroing the boundary.

This may read an entire large folio back from swap while holding
i_rwsem, only to discard part of it. Avoiding that I/O would require
splitting both the swap entry and any large folio still in the swap
cache. That, however, is much bigger work.

summary: ksmbd: fix NULL pointer dereference in session_user_name() and session_account_type()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix NULL pointer dereference in session_user_name() and session_account_type()

session_user_name() and session_account_type() dereference
session->user without checking for NULL. A session can be published
and exposed via the procfs session interface before authentication
completes, during which session->user is NULL:

  show_proc_session() -> session_user_name(sess)
    -> user_guest(session->user) -> NULL->flags -> oops

Guard both functions by treating a NULL session->user as an explicit
not-yet-authenticated state rather than dereferencing it.

summary: mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: map the shared tail page writable

page_ref_add_unless_zero() reads the refcount and then updates it with a
cmpxchg.  A lockless get, such as a page cache lookup or a PFN scanner,
can read a non-zero refcount from a page that is then freed and reused as
a hugetlb tail page.  If HVO remaps its struct page to the shared tail
page in between, the cmpxchg writes to read-only vmemmap:

    CPU0 (lockless get)               CPU1
    c = atomic_read(&page->_refcount)
                                      page freed
                                      page allocated as a hugetlb tail
                                      HVO remaps the struct page RO
    try_cmpxchg(&page->_refcount, &c, c + 1)
      -> write fault on read-only vmemmap

The refcount is zero by then and the compare fails, but a compare-and-swap
instruction needs write access whether or not it succeeds.  The kernel
oopses when hugetlb pages are allocated at runtime with HVO enabled while
a lockless get races with it.

Commit bd225530a4c7 ("mm/hugetlb_vmemmap: fix race with speculative PFN
walkers") closed the window with RCU on both sides.  The RCU was removed
together with fake heads, on the wrong belief that it was only needed for
them.

Map the shared tail page writable instead of restoring the RCU.  Every
struct page on it is a tail with a zero refcount, so a late cmpxchg
fails and leaves the page unchanged.  RCU would put rcu_read_lock()
back around every get and synchronize_rcu() back into hugetlb
allocation and freeing.

The cost is the protection against stray writes to tail struct pages.  The
shared page is shared by all hugetlb folios of the same order in the zone,
so such a write now corrupts all of them instead of oopsing.

Bootmem folios optimized when the memmap is set up keep their tails
read-only.  Nothing does a lockless get on them before hugetlb takes them
over.

summary: HID: mcp2200: validate READ_ALL response length
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: mcp2200: validate READ_ALL response length

The HID core invokes raw_event callbacks before validating the report
length.  mcp2200_raw_event() casts a READ_ALL response to struct
mcp_read_all_resp and reads fields through offset ten without checking that
the response contains the structure.

A one-byte READ_ALL response reproduced the issue under KASAN:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0
  Read of size 1 by task hidtrigger/89
  Call Trace:
   mcp2200_raw_event+0x24b/0x3a0
   kasan_report+0x139/0x170

Reject an incomplete READ_ALL response with a protocol error before reading
its fields.  The common completion path then wakes the command waiter with
the error instead of leaving it to time out.

Commit 47669bec44fe ("HID: asus: refactor the two workqueues and init
sequence") added the same kind of raw_event length validation to hid-asus.

summary: PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

PM: EM: Fix use-after-free of perf domain in netlink doit handlers

The doit handlers dropped em_pd_list_mutex before dereferencing the
perf domain, so a concurrent device unregister could free it while the
reply was being built.

Encode the reply from em_perf_domain_for_id() callbacks, which run
under the mutex, and allocate the skb outside of it, like the dumpit
path already does.

This issue was found by an in-house static analysis tool.

summary: net/9p/usbg: call disable_usb9pfs() from usb9pfs_disable()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: call disable_usb9pfs() from usb9pfs_disable()

usb9pfs_disable() is the usb_function ->disable callback, invoked by
the composite gadget core whenever the host resets or unconfigures
the gadget. The gadget function API requires this callback to disable
its endpoints; every other in-tree function driver does so from its
->disable hook.

usb9pfs_disable() never called disable_usb9pfs(), so the IN/OUT
endpoints and their usb_request objects were left active and
allocated across a host-driven disable. When the host later
reconfigures the device, enable_usb9pfs() calls alloc_requests() again
and unconditionally overwrites usb9pfs->in_req/out_req, permanently
leaking the previous allocations, while the endpoints themselves are
left enabled underneath the function's own idea of being disabled.

Call disable_usb9pfs() before reinit_completion(&usb9pfs->send),
mirroring the same sequence already used in p9_usbg_close(). Placing
it before the reinit_completion() also ensures usb_ep_disable() has
synchronously flushed any requests still queued in hardware before the
completion is reset, closing the same race that motivated resetting
the completion here in the first place.

summary: fs/proc/task_mmu: pin mm_users in do_pagemap_scan()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fs/proc/task_mmu: pin mm_users in do_pagemap_scan()

The PAGEMAP_SCAN ioctl takes mmap_read_lock() on an mm obtained from
/proc/<pid>/pagemap without holding a reference to mm_users.

proc_mem_open() deliberately grabs only mm_count, so a consumer that
touches the address space has to call mmget_not_zero() first.  Every other
consumer in this file does -- m_start(), do_procmap_query(),
show_smaps_rollup() and pagemap_read() -- but do_pagemap_scan() does not.

Without that reference the target can reach exit_mmap() concurrently, and
exit_mmap() calls unmap_vmas() while holding mmap_lock only for reading,
which does not exclude the scanner.  For ordinary VMAs this is harmless,
as free_pgtables() and remove_vma() run afterwards under mmap_write_lock. 
A shared hugetlb VMA is different: __hugetlb_zap_end() frees the VMA's
hugetlb_vma_lock inside the read-locked phase.

walk_hugetlb_range() can therefore load vma->vm_private_data, have the
lock freed underneath it, and then down_read() a freed rw_semaphore.  The
load happens before the freeing side clears the pointer, so this is a
use-after-free and not a NULL dereference.  Any unprivileged user can
reach it with no huge pages configured, as hugetlb_reserve_pages()
allocates the lock before the VM_NORESERVE early return.

Pin mm_users across the scan, the way the other consumers do.  mmput()
from the exiting task can then no longer reach exit_mmap() while a walk is
in progress.

[akpm@linux-foundation.org: remove unneeded & undesirable test for !mm]

summary: smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: fix early procfs exposure race

Currently, init_cifs() calls cifs_proc_init() near the beginning of
the function, before INIT_LIST_HEAD, leading to a momentarily
uninitialized, but exposed, procfs. If a userspace process reads this
empty procfs, iterating over a zeroed list_head leads to a NULL
pointer dereference and a kernel oops/panic.

For example, if a delay is added between cifs_proc_init() and
INIT_LIST_HEAD, and a userspace process is polling
/proc/fs/cifs/DebugData, the following oops occurs:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000608
Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP PTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 3477 Comm: cat Not tainted
7.3.0-02212-g4df4d2a577db-dirty #6 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:cifs_debug_data_proc_show+0x103/0xd80 [cifs]
Call Trace:
<TASK>
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 ? seq_read_iter+0x86/0x400
 seq_read_iter+0x183/0x400
 proc_reg_read_iter+0x62/0x90
 copy_splice_read+0x215/0x310
 splice_file_to_pipe+0xec/0x1c0
 do_splice+0x4b8/0x780
 __se_sys_splice+0x18f/0x250
 do_syscall_64+0x109/0x330
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
</TASK>

Fix this by moving cifs_proc_init() down in init_cifs(), ensuring it runs
only after all internal lists, locks, counters, and workqueues are fully
ready, but before registering the filesystem. Update the error cleanup
ladder and exit_cifs() to maintain proper LIFO order.

summary: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast

The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to
start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated
the length on 32bit.

Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts
from a 64-bit userspace length.

Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with
-EOVERFLOW early.

summary: platform/x86: asus-wmi: fix use-after-free unregistering kbd_led led
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

platform/x86: asus-wmi: fix use-after-free unregistering kbd_led led

kbd_led_update_all() registers asus->kbd_led with
devm_led_classdev_register() on the platform device, but kbd_led is
embedded in struct asus_wmi, which asus_wmi_remove() frees at its end.
The driver core calls .remove() before devres_release_all(), so the
deferred devres release runs led_classdev_unregister() on memory that
has already been freed. Whether that faults depends on whether the
slab has been reused in between, which makes the crash on module
unload intermittent and silently corrupts the led classdev state in
the remaining runs.

Unregister the led classdev explicitly in asus_wmi_led_exit(), after
the led workqueue has been destroyed: kbd_led_work can then neither
run nor be queued anymore, since asus_ref.asus is NULL too, so
kbd_led_registered is stable and the classdev can be released while
the memory embedding it is still alive. devm_led_classdev_unregister()
also drops the devres entry, leaving nothing to run at unbind cleanup
time; it warns when no devres entry exists, hence the
kbd_led_registered check.

summary: serial: core: shut down initialized port on removal
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

serial: core: shut down initialized port on removal

When a serial port configured as a console is opened and subsequently
closed, tty_port_shutdown() skips invoking port->ops->shutdown() because
port->console is true. As a result, tty_port_initialized() remains true
and the port's interrupt handler stays registered in the irq subsystem.

If the underlying device is later unbound or removed (e.g. via sysfs
driver unbind or device hot-unplug), serial_core_remove_one_port()
unregisters the console, frees uport->name via kfree(), and tears down
the port without shutting it down or freeing its IRQ. Consequently, the
irqaction descriptor remains registered in genirq with action->name
pointing to freed memory.

This triggers a use-after-free read whenever genirq accesses action->name,
such as when reading /proc/interrupts:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in string+0x476/0x570
  Call Trace:
   string+0x476/0x570
   vsnprintf+0x422/0x1300
   seq_printf+0x...
   show_interrupts+...

Fix this by acquiring port->mutex in serial_core_remove_one_port() after
console unregistration, clearing port->console under the mutex to prevent
data races with concurrent tty_port_shutdown(), and invoking
uart_shutdown(NULL, state) if the port remains initialized. This ensures
that port->ops->shutdown() is called and the IRQ is freed before
kfree(uport->name).

summary: can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: raw, isotp: copy socket options outside of lock_sock()

The CAN_RAW and CAN_ISOTP specific socket options are copied from and
to user space while holding lock_sock(). A copy that faults or stalls,
e.g. on a userfaultfd or FUSE backed mapping, holds lock_sock() for its
whole duration.

raw_notify() and isotp_notify() take lock_sock() of a socket that is
bound to the vanishing device while holding RTNL. As the CAN_RAW
options can also be changed on a bound socket, a stalled copy can block
RTNL on an unregistration or namespace change of the bound device.
Before "can: protect the receive lists with a per-device lock",
raw_setsockopt() even held RTNL itself during the copy. CAN_ISOTP only
copies its options for unbound sockets, which isotp_notify() skips
without taking lock_sock().

Keep the user space copies out of the locked sections: Check the option
name and length and copy the option values, including the CAN_RAW_FILTER
filters, to kernel memory before lock_sock(). raw_setsockopt_locked()
and isotp_setsockopt_locked() get the copied values directly and drop
their now redundant length checks and copies. As a side effect, a
failing copy can not leave partially overwritten options behind
anymore. In raw_getsockopt() duplicate the filters under lock_sock() and
copy them to user space after release_sock().

As the option name and length are now checked before lock_sock(), the
order of the checks in isotp_setsockopt() and accordingly the order of
the returned error values changes. This is in line with POSIX, which
does not define an order in which multiple error conditions are
detected and reported.

The generic SOL_SOCKET options in sk_setsockopt() are not affected by
this patch.

summary: net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/9p/usbg: clear stale client pointer on close

p9_usbg_close() tears down the client transport, but usb9pfs keeps
using usb9pfs->client from asynchronous TX and RX completion handlers.
A late completion can therefore dereference a client that has already
been freed during mount teardown.

Clear usb9pfs->client under usb9pfs->lock when closing the transport,
detach any pending TX request from in_req->context, and make the TX/RX
completion handlers bail out once the transport has been detached. This
keeps late completions from touching a freed or rebound p9_client.

summary: s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup

zpci_remove_parent_msi_domain() dereferences zbus->msi_parent_domain
unconditionally and does not clear it afterwards.

zpci_bus_create_pci_bus() removes the domain when pci_create_root_bus()
fails, then zpci_bus_release() removes it again on the last kref_put(),
reading ->fwnode from the freed irq_domain and freeing it twice.

If zpci_alloc_domain() or zpci_create_parent_msi_domain() fails, no domain
is created at all; zbus is kzalloc'd, so the same release path dereferences
NULL.

Return early when there is no domain, and clear the pointer after removing
one.

summary: 9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p: don't decrement a server-owned zero nlink

A 9P2000.L server can report nlink=0 for a regular file that still
exists.  On a cache=loose or cache=fscache mount, lookup stores that
value with set_nlink().  A later successful unlink calls
v9fs_dec_count(), which still calls drop_nlink() for a non-directory.
drop_nlink() warns, and the unsigned link count wraps to 4294967295.
fstat() on a descriptor opened before the unlink shows 0 before and
4294967295 after.

The warning on the unpatched kernel, trimmed:

WARNING: fs/inode.c:408 at drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0, CPU#1: trigger/188
CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 188 Comm: trigger Tainted: G                 N  7.3.0-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
RIP: 0010:drop_nlink+0xac/0xd0
Call Trace:
 <TASK>
 v9fs_remove+0x529/0x750
 vfs_unlink+0x2f0/0xbd0
 filename_unlinkat+0x340/0x6c0
 __x64_sys_unlink+0x46/0x70
 do_syscall_64+0xe8/0x4f0
 entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x77/0x7f
 </TASK>
---[ end trace 0000000000000000 ]---

Directories whose cached nlink is at most 2 already skip this
decrement, because the exported filesystem may not maintain nlink
(commit ac89b2ef9b559).  cache=none skips it as well (commit
574aa0b479947).  cache=mmap does not take this path: it sets neither
CACHE_META nor CACHE_LOOSE.  A regular file on cache=loose or
cache=fscache still does.  Its count came from GETATTR and may
already be zero, so skip the decrement when i_nlink is already 0.

Verified on 7.3-rc4-00537-ga3ff15db6820 with only this change.  A
server that advertises nlink=0 and accepts the unlink no longer
warns, and the open descriptor stays at nlink 0.  An honest server
on the same mount still goes from 1 to 0.  A rejected unlink leaves
the count unchanged.  cache=none is unchanged.  With panic_on_warn
the unpatched kernel panics on the warning; the patched kernel does
not.

summary: mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: recheck the PUD under PTL in follow_pud_mask()

follow_pud_mask() reads the PUD without a lock. If it is a leaf, it takes
the lock and calls follow_huge_pud(), which reads the entry again, but
only tests whether it is present.

A leaf can be zapped concurrently and a page fault can fill the empty
entry with a page table.

This currently only applies when device-dax makes use of PUD entries,
and the fault after e.g., MADV_DONTNEED would find THPs to be disabled.

That requires a sequence like

1) Fault in the PUD
2) Disable THP
3) Have GUP race against concurrent MADV_DONTNEED + refault

Which is rather unlikely to happen in practice, which is why we never
received a report about such a problem.

Before commit 1b1676180246 ("mm/gup: handle huge pud for
follow_pud_mask()"), we performed that check in follow_devmap_pud() by
testing for pud_devmap().

Let's fix it by just structuring follow_pud_mask() similar to
follow_pmd_mask(), minus protnone stuff that does not apply and minus
FOLL_SPLIT_PMD handling. That makes it much easier to spot any such
inconsistencies.

Perform the pud_bad() check early in follow_pmd_mask() and just forward
the PUD value. We can drop the pud_present() check in follow_huge_pud(),
just like we have in follow_huge_pmd().

Even though we are performing more changes than strictly necessary, the
fix should be easy to backport.

summary: ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: don't allow compression on volumes with clusters larger than 4K

On a volume made with "mkntfs -c 8192", a user can set
FILE_ATTR_COMPRESSED on an empty file through system.ntfs_attrib.
Writing to the file and reading it back after dropping the page cache
then crashes:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in ntfs_read_compressed_block+0xa2c/0x2040
  Read of size 8192 at addr ffff88804355a000 by task dd/106

The read path only handles clusters up to 4K. It copies each cluster
out of a single page, and a compression block of 16 8K clusters does
not fit in the 64K ntfs_compression_buffer. Loading an inode already
rejects compressed data on such volumes.

Reject the flag change the same way.

summary: mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix clearing folios in memfd_pin_folios()

memfd_pin_folios() pins folios obtained directly from the page cache
without checking whether they are uptodate. However, shmem fallocate()
can leave newly allocated folios uncleared and not uptodate. Callers
such as udmabuf can then expose uninitialized memory to userspace.

Clear non-uptodate folios and mark them uptodate under the folio lock
before returning them to the caller.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description and comment ]

summary: sunrpc: pin gss module across auth_domain RCU free
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sunrpc: pin gss module across auth_domain RCU free

A gss auth_domain stores a raw pointer to svcauthops_gss in
dom->flavour, and its release queues svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu()
via call_rcu(). Both live in auth_rpcgss.ko text, and nothing pins the
module while a domain referencing it is reachable. rmmod auth_rpcgss
can therefore unmap that text while an NFSD export still holds a
reference to the domain.

The export cache is one such holder. When the export is finally
released, the domain reference drops from module text:

    svc_export_put()
      auth_domain_put(exp->ex_client)
        auth_domain_release()
          dom->flavour->domain_release(dom)   /* into module text */
            svcauth_gss_domain_release()
              call_rcu(&dom->rcu_head,
                       svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu)

Once auth_rpcgss is unloaded, the domain_release call lands in
unmapped memory. The rcu_barrier() in exit_rpcsec_gss() does not
help: it waits only for callbacks already queued, and this one is
not queued until the export goes away.

NFSD's NFSv4 objects import symbols from auth_rpcgss.ko, so only a
server built without CONFIG_NFSD_V4 can unload auth_rpcgss while
exports still name a gss domain.

Take a module reference in svcauth_gss_register_pseudoflavor() before
publishing the domain and drop it at the end of
svcauth_gss_domain_release_rcu(). The rcu_barrier() then holds the
module image until this callback has returned.

[ cel: rewrote description ]

summary: KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86/mmu: Conditionally resched when retrying gPTE walk on A/D update failure

Conditionally reschedule when retrying a guest PTE walk because the CMPXCHG
to update A/D bits failed, e.g. because a different task/vCPU modified the
relevant gPTEs.  On kernels without involuntary preemption of some kind, a
misbehaving guest can "capture" a pCPU effectively indefinitely and trigger
soft lockups by continuously modifying its gPTEs such that the result of
the walk is remains valid.

summary: s390/zcrypt: Fix and improve zcrypt reply message verification checks
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/zcrypt: Fix and improve zcrypt reply message verification checks

Add or improve checks related to buffer sizes and reply sizes to the
handling of replies from the crypto cards for CCA, EP11 (AP message
type 6) and ICA (AP type 50) messages. The verification code related
to reply field length was not designed well and thus firmware
deficiencies could lead to unexpected behavior in the zcrypt device
driver. Thus improve the code to more closely inspect especially
length fields at message replies.

Add length validation before accessing reply message structures in
zcrypt_msgtype6_receive(), zcrypt_msgtype6_receive_ep11(), and
zcrypt_msgtype50_receive() to prevent out-of-bounds reads and
potential kernel memory disclosure.

Also rework these three functions to validate reply lengths more
carefully before copying data back into the request buffer. Use size_t
for length calculations, reject inconsistent reply sizes, and add
defensive handling for short invalid replies. For XCRB replies,
validate both reply segments and derive the effective message length
from the covered range instead of trusting only the second segment.

Additionally improve some of the later invoked evaluation functions
which further check the payload. Add comments about length assumptions
and for the type50 processing rework the payload processing completely
with removing a misplaced BUG_ON().

summary: mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: always recheck the pmd in try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp()

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() drops the PTE lock after it has cleared the
page table, and takes the PMD lock and the PTE lock to remove it.

In between, MADV_DONTNEED with CONFIG_PT_RECLAIM can reclaim the
page table. The pmd_same() check is supposed to handle this, but it is
only done with CONFIG_SPLIT_PTE_PTLOCKS.

Fix it by performing the check unconditionally.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: adjust description ]

summary: genirq: Defer kfree(irqaction) until irq_thread_dtor() finishes
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

genirq: Defer kfree(irqaction) until irq_thread_dtor() finishes

When an interrupt thread exits abnormally via do_exit() (e.g. the interrupt
handler oopses) without returning from irq_thread(), a concurrent call to
free_irq() could free the irqaction before the irq_thread_dtor() exit task
work runs.

  irq thread (oopsed)                 free_irq()
  -------------------                 ----------
  do_exit()
    exit_mm()
      complete_vfork_done()  -------> kthread_stop() returns
    exit_files() ...                  kfree(action)
    exit_task_work()
      irq_thread_dtor()
        action->...                   <- use-after-free

Track the pending exit work with the IRQTF_EXIT_WORK thread flag, and have
__free_irq() wait for the bit to clear before kfree().

irq_thread_dtor() only runs on irq_thread abnormal exit. If that dtor also
faults, free_irq() will hang indefinitely, but double IRQ thread faults
require a reboot anyways.

[ tglx: Add missing include ]

summary: drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/loongson: Fix double free on BO initialization failure

If ttm_bo_init_validate() fails, it drops the buffer object's reference
and cleans it up through the supplied destroy callback. lsdc_bo_destroy()
releases the GEM object and frees the enclosing lsdc_bo, so freeing it
again in lsdc_bo_create() causes a double free on a synchronous failure
path.

Let TTM own the cleanup after initialization has started and return the
error directly. Keep the explicit free on drm_gem_object_init() failure,
which occurs before ownership is passed to TTM.

Tested on LS7A2000 by making drm_vma_offset_add() return -ENOSPC for one
selected dumb-buffer creation. The error reached userspace, the destroy
callback ran once, and no handle was published or tracked BO retained.
Normal buffer creation, zeroing, mapping, readback and release passed.

AI assistance was used for the ownership analysis, fix, fault-injection
tools, build and test execution.

summary: hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

hwrng: virtio - prevent use-after-free after a failed restore

remove_common() frees the driver data during freeze, but does not clear
vdev->priv, which points to freed memory. If probe_common() then fails
during restore, a later remove or freeze can dereference the dangling
pointer.

Clear vdev->priv on the probe_common() error cleanup path and before
freeing the driver data in remove_common(). Also reset the device and
return early from remove_common() if vdev->priv is already NULL for a
safe teardown after a failed restore.

summary: KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Conditionally resched when restarting REP string emulation

When restarting emulation, e.g. of a REP-prefixed string instruction,
conditionally reschedule as emulating guest writes can be deceptively slow
and expensive, e.g. when shadow paging is in use and each write can trigger
write tracking.

In a perfect world, restarting emulation (or not) would be less arbitrary,
e.g. would honor not only host events (NEED_RESCHED, signals, etc.) but
also guest events (e.g. by checking kvm_vcpu_has_events()).  Unfortunately,
as pointed out by Sashiko, pio_in_emulated()'s read-ahead logic is baked
into the restart logic, as KVM relies on restarting emulation to drain the
cache and avoid duplicate reads from the I/O port.  I.e. re-entering the
guest on kvm_vcpu_has_events() or __xfer_to_guest_mode_work_pending() would
introduce architecturally-incorrect, guest-visible changes.

summary: xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfrm: interface: validate the IP header on xmit

Packets injected into an xfrm interface (e.g. AF_PACKET on an xfrmi
device) reach the xfrm output path without IP header validation, but
xfrm4_transport_output() uses iph->ihl for __skb_pull() and memmove()
and expects the header to be valid.

vti_tunnel_xmit() already calls pskb_inet_may_pull() before handing
packets to the xfrm output path.  Do the same in xfrmi_xmit() and
perform the header checks ip_rcv_core()/ip6_rcv_core() do on entry
to the IP stack: reject wrong IP versions and malformed IPv4 header
lengths.

summary: btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

btrfs: sysfs: restore NOFS context on early return in btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type()

btrfs_sysfs_add_block_group_type() sets up a NOFS context with
memalloc_nofs_save() because kobject_add() performs GFP_KERNEL
allocations deep in its call chain, and the function may be called
while holding a transaction handle or a lock required for a
transaction commit, where reclaim could deadlock.

Every other return path of this function calls memalloc_nofs_restore()
except the early return taken when another thread has already created
the kobject for the same raid index (this can happen when restriping).
Taking that path leaves PF_MEMALLOC_NOFS set on the calling task, so
all subsequent memory allocations performed by that task remain
restricted to the NOFS scope, which may lead to unexpected allocation
failures or deadlocks later on.

Restore the NOFS context before returning from that path.

summary: nvmet: fix use-after-free of the old registrant in nvmet_pr_preempt()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet: fix use-after-free of the old registrant in nvmet_pr_preempt()

nvmet_pr_preempt() handles a preempt sent by the reservation holder by
changing the reservation type with nvmet_pr_update_reg_attr(), unless
the reservation is of an All Registrants type.  For the holder that
helper does not modify the registrant in place: it puts a copy on the
registrant list, points pr->holder to the copy and passes the old
registrant to kfree_rcu().

If the reservation type changed, nvmet_pr_preempt() then hands
&reg->hostid of that old registrant to nvmet_pr_resv_released().  Unless
the reservation released notification is masked, that function takes
subsys->lock and compares the host id against every controller of the
subsystem.  The caller only holds pr->pr_sem and is not in an RCU
read-side critical section, so nothing keeps the old registrant alive
while it is read.

The result is a read of 16 freed bytes that decides which controllers
get the notification.  Found by code inspection.  kfree_rcu() defers
the free, so it usually happens after the read; when the pending free
is forced to run before the read, KASAN reports the host id as freed
memory.

Pass the host id of the controller that sent the command instead.  The
registrant was looked up by that host id, and the controller outlives
the request.

summary: backlight: qcom-wled: Fix NULL pointer dereference in wled_remove()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

backlight: qcom-wled: Fix NULL pointer dereference in wled_remove()

wled_probe() doesn't set the driver data for the platform device.
As a result, platform_get_drvdata() in wled_remove() will return NULL,
and the first dereference of it crashes on unbind.

Set the platform device driver data in wled_probe().

summary: filelock: keep superblock active through delegation wait
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

filelock: keep superblock active through delegation wait

A caller may drop its path after try_break_deleg() returns a delegated
inode but before break_deleg_wait() finishes. The extra inode reference
held in struct delegated_inode does not keep the superblock active.

After a lazy unmount, closing the delegation holder can release the last
mount reference and shut down the superblock while another task waits for
the delegation break. The waiter's final iput() can then enter the
filesystem's eviction code after its superblock-private state was freed.
This has been observed as a KASAN use-after-free in shmem_evict_inode().

When try_break_deleg() saves a delegated inode, take an active reference
to its superblock while the caller still pins the mount. Keep that
reference through break_deleg_wait() and the final iput(), then release
it with deactivate_super(). This protects every caller of the helpers,
including the mknod, mkdir, symlink and rmdir paths that drop their path
before waiting.

summary: ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2: stop recovery before shutting down local allocators

Recovery completion needs the local allocators until it has finished
reclaiming a failed node's allocation window and truncate log.  During
unmount, quota recovery is stopped first, but that leaves recovery_state
at OCFS2_REC_QUOTA_DISABLED.  New non-quota recovery can still start.

ocfs2_truncate_log_shutdown() drains existing completion work and releases
osb_tl_bh before ocfs2_recovery_exit() closes that publication path:

  Unmount                             Recovery
  -------                             --------
  stop quota recovery; disable quotas
  truncate_log_shutdown()
    flush existing completion work
                                      recover another failed node
                                        queue completion
    flush local log; release buffer
                                      complete_truncate_log_recovery()
                                        use released osb_tl_bh
  recovery_exit(): disable and drain

An extra buffer reference alone would still let completion append new
records after the final truncate-log flush.

Split stopping and draining recovery from freeing its state. Stop all
recovery producers and drain completion work before shutting down either
local allocator. Keep recovery-state release at its existing later point,
so its lifetime relative to other teardown users stays unchanged. The
second stop at recovery_exit() is harmless once recovery is disabled.

KASAN report as below:

summary: mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: preserve dirty bits when collapsing PTE-mapped THPs

try_collapse_pte_mapped_thp() clears PTEs without transferring their dirty
bits to the folio. A shmem read fault can map a clean folio writable, so
a later store only dirties the PTE. Losing that dirty bit allows reclaim
to discard modified data.

The assumption that regular files are read-only is also obsolete since
commit 1b6444331bebb ("mm/khugepaged: enable clean pagecache folio collapse
for writable files"). In any case, transferring PTE dirty bits to the folio
when removing mappings (and while the folio is still mapped) is the right
thing to do.

Use get_and_clear_ptes() to collect the dirty bits and mark the folio
dirty before unmapping it. Update the comment.

This was reproduced with shmem using MADV_COLLAPSE followed by
MADV_PAGEOUT.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: adjust comment; simplify description; cover file-thp as well ]

summary: rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust_binder: wake epoll on self-work queued to poll thread

When a thread pushes work to its own todo list, InnerThread::push_work()
returns PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll if the thread uses epoll, but four
call sites in thread.rs discard this return value. As a result, a
non-blocking BC_* write that enqueues work onto the calling thread's
todo list without also reading will not wake epoll. Check the return
value and call self.process.notify_poll(false) when
PushWorkRes::OkNotifyPoll is returned.

This is similar to commit 97830f3c3088 ("binder: signal epoll threads of
self-work"), but in C Binder pending thread work also prevented
subsequent process work from waking epoll, causing a permanent hang,
which is not the case in Rust Binder. This means that in practice, it
merely delays notifications rather than completely failing to send them.

summary: mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm: fix address wraparound when scanning large folio PTEs

numa_rebuild_large_mapping() and do_swap_page() can be tricked into
generating an address wraparound, crashing the kernel. All that's required
is to map a tail page of a large folio close enough to the start/end of
the address space to e.g., make

	unsigned long addr_start = addr - (nr << PAGE_SHIFT);

to wrap around.

Let's fix it by providing a better helper, folio_scan_range(), that
takes care of staying within VMA and page table boundaries while
handling possible wraparounds.

There are some nasty details, like not being able to use pmd_addr_end()
in this context. Add some helpful comments for these cases.

summary: ALSA: x86: hdmi: fix chmap array missing terminator entry
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: x86: hdmi: fix chmap array missing terminator entry

had_build_channel_allocation_map() allocates a single struct
snd_pcm_chmap_elem via kzalloc() and stores it as
intelhaddata->chmap->chmap. struct snd_pcm_chmap.chmap is expected to
be a zero-terminated array (see snd_pcm_std_chmaps[]), but
had_register_chmap_ctls() never overrides the TLV callback installed
by snd_pcm_add_chmap_ctls(), so the generic pcm_chmap_ctl_tlv() from
ALSA core is left in place.

pcm_chmap_ctl_tlv() is reachable by any local user via
SNDRV_CTL_IOCTL_TLV_READ on the "Playback Channel Map" control and
walks the array with "for (map = info->chmap; map->channels; map++)".
Since the driver's single element is never terminated, this walks
past the allocation. The same pointer is also freed on hot-unplug and
rebuilt on hot-plug under intelhaddata->mutex, while the TLV callback
runs under card->controls_rwsem without that mutex, so the walk can
also race a concurrent free of the array.

Fix this by allocating a second, zeroed element so the array is
properly terminated, and by dropping the inherited TLV callback
entirely at registration time, since the driver never implements one
of its own.

summary: ptp: fix use-after-free in extts_fifo_show() reading tsevqs unlocked
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ptp: fix use-after-free in extts_fifo_show() reading tsevqs unlocked

extts_fifo_show() walks ptp->tsevqs with list_count_nodes() and then
list_first_entry() without holding ptp->tsevqs_lock, the spinlock that
"protects tsevqs from concurrent access". Every other accessor of the
list honours it: ptp_open() (list_add_tail), ptp_release() (list_del
followed by kfree of the per-fd queue), ptp_clock_release() and
ptp_clock_event() all take tsevqs_lock. extts_fifo_show() is the only
one that does not.

A per-fd timestamp queue is appended to tsevqs on open("/dev/ptpN") and
removed and freed on close(), both under tsevqs_lock:

	scoped_guard(spinlock_irq, &ptp->tsevqs_lock)
		list_del(&queue->qlist);
	bitmap_free(queue->mask);
	kfree(queue);

So a read of /sys/class/ptp/ptpN/fifo running concurrently with a
close() of a /dev/ptpN fd can have list_count_nodes() walk into the
queue that close() is removing and freeing, dereferencing freed memory
(use-after-free) or a poisoned list pointer.

Take tsevqs_lock around the list walk. The fifo only ever draws from the
first queue, which is the registration-time queue created in
ptp_clock_register() and freed only in ptp_clock_release(); that cannot
run while the sysfs attribute is being read, so the dequeue from
queue->buf under queue->lock may stay outside tsevqs_lock and the lock
order is unchanged.

summary: mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

summary: ksmbd: grant a POSIX ACL group entry only to the group's members
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: grant a POSIX ACL group entry only to the group's members

When no ACE of the DACL matches the caller, Everyone or Authenticated
Users, smb_check_perm_dacl() falls back to the file's POSIX ACL. It
takes the first ACL_USER or ACL_GROUP entry whose id equals the
caller's uid. For ACL_GROUP, this compares a gid with the caller's uid.
A numerical match grants the group's permissions even when the caller
is not a member.

Match a group entry only when the caller is also in the group.

summary: xfs: complain loudly when dirtree checker finds broken links
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: complain loudly when dirtree checker finds broken links

LOLLM observed that the directory tree walk code bails out if it finds
broken parent pointers along the way.  However, it flattens the return
code to zero, which means that we can end up in the repair code having
not completed the scan.  We should never proceed with a repair in this
state, so let's mark the scrub incomplete and exit.

summary: NFSD: Don't complete a cld upcall the daemon has not read
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Don't complete a cld upcall the daemon has not read

cld_pipe_downcall() matches a reply to its upcall on the xid alone.
A write that arrives before the daemon has read that upcall
completes __cld_pipe_upcall() while its struct rpc_pipe_msg is still
queued on the pipe. The waiter returns, its stack frame goes away,
and the pipe keeps a list_head that points into it. The next
rpc_queue_upcall() walks that pointer:

  BUG: KASAN: vmalloc-out-of-bounds in __list_add_valid_or_report
  Read of size 8 at addr ffffc90007027950 by task syz.0.96/13066
   __list_add_valid_or_report+0x6a/0x130
   rpc_queue_upcall
   cld_pipe_upcall
   nfsd4_cld_grace_start
   nfsd4_cld_tracking_init

The pipe is mode 0600 in rpc_pipefs, so the trigger is a broken or
hostile nfsdcld rather than an unprivileged task.

Record whether the daemon has consumed the whole message and
complete only when it has. cld_pipe_destroy_msg() runs on every path
by which the pipe releases a message, so it can maintain that flag
under cn_lock. nfsdcld sends its -EINPROGRESS downcalls only after
reading the upcall, so the new check does not break the GraceStart
record stream.

summary: pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed

Once blkmapd has read a whole upcall, rpc_pipe_read() unlinks the
message from every pipe list, so the purges in rpc_pipe_release()
and rpc_close_pipes() no longer reach it. bl_upcall_ops supplies no
.release_pipe callback, and bl_pipe_destroy_msg() returns without
completing the upcall because a downcall is expected to follow. A
daemon that exits between the read and the write therefore strands
its waiter: bl_resolve_deviceid() sleeps in wait_for_completion()
and never returns, and it holds nn->bl_mutex across that wait, so
every later device resolution in the net namespace blocks behind
it.

Add a .release_pipe that completes an upcall blkmapd has consumed
and left unanswered. Completing an upcall retires it, so a message
the framework has already purged is no longer in flight and is not
completed a second time here.

summary: mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/userfaultfd: write-lock the VMA before waking waiters when unregistering

userfaultfd_unregister() wakes pending missing faults before clearing the
VMA's userfaultfd registration. With per-VMA fault locking, holding
mmap_lock for write does not prevent another fault from queuing after
the wakeup but before userfaultfd_clear_vma() write-locks the VMA. That
waiter can then remain asleep indefinitely.

Call vma_start_write() before waking waiters. Existing fault handlers
queue themselves before dropping the VMA read lock, and new readers are
excluded until mmap_write_unlock().

summary: can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

can: dev: can_dropped_invalid_skb: drop CAN XL frames on non-CAN XL devices

Sending a PF_PACKET bypasses the CAN framework logic and can directly
reach a CAN driver's xmit() function. The PF_PACKET framework only
checks that skb->len does not exceed the net_device MTU.

For a CAN device that is not CAN XL capable, anything above CANFD_MTU
(72 bytes) is therefore dropped before it reaches the driver. However,
CAN XL frames are variable length. can_is_canxl_skb() accepts lengths in
the range CANXL_HDR_SIZE + CANXL_MIN_DLEN up to CANXL_MTU, i.e. 13 to
2060 bytes.

As a result, an ETH_P_CANXL skb with a length between 13 and 72 bytes
can pass both the MTU and the can_dropped_invalid_skb() checks.

A driver that does not support CAN XL will interpret canxl_frame->flags
as a length because of the overlap with can_frame->len. And because
CANXL_XLF is set, the resulting length is between 128 and 255. For
drivers that do not check can_frame->len before copying can_frame->data,
as most drivers do, this results in a buffer overflow of up to 247
bytes.

Drop ETH_P_CANXL skbs if the device does not have the CAN_CAP_XL
capability. Keep can_is_canxl_skb() for the validation of CAN XL skbs.

summary: NFSD: Destroy a recalled delegation the client does not hold
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSD: Destroy a recalled delegation the client does not hold

A client that answers CB_RECALL with NFS4ERR_BADHANDLE or
NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID has no record of the delegation, so the
FREE_STATEID that clears it from cl_revoked never arrives. Every later
SEQUENCE reply carries SEQ4_STATUS_RECALLABLE_STATE_REVOKED, and the
client loops issuing TEST_STATEID.

Destroy such a delegation when it is reaped rather than revoking it
onto cl_revoked. RFC 8881 Section 20.2.4 completes the recall at the
reply when its status is neither NFS4_OK nor NFS4ERR_DELAY, so a
rejected recall leaves nothing to revoke. An administrative revoke
keeps that path, since NFS4ERR_ADMIN_REVOKED reports it. A destroyed
stateid returns NFS4ERR_BAD_STATEID instead of NFS4ERR_DELEG_REVOKED. A
client that rejects the recall but still holds the delegation gets no
notice that its state was revoked.

CB_RECALL can outrun the reply that granted the delegation, so honor
a rejection only once the client has seen that grant. Per RFC 8881
Section 2.10.6.3, retirement of the slot that carried the grant is that
proof; retry until then, and revoke when the retries lapse.

summary: ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

summary: mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mempolicy: charge shared policy nodes

Any local user can bypass memory.max with mbind() on a tmpfs file, and
allocate unbounded kernel memory.

mbind() sets a NUMA memory policy for a range of a mapping. If the
mapping is of a shmem and friends, the kernel also stores the policy on
the inode, in a tree with one entry per range of the file.

Each mbind() on a single page of a mapping can add one shared policy node
(struct sp_node) and one struct mempolicy to that tree. They outlive the
mapping and stay around until the inode is destroyed. The tree is not
bounded by the file size, so the file can be empty.

Memory that user space can allocate must be charged to a memory cgroup. A
slab cache does that for all of its objects if it is created with
SLAB_ACCOUNT. numa_policy_init() creates the slab caches for both
structs without SLAB_ACCOUNT, so they are not charged to any cgroup.

Reproduced with mbind() on single pages of an empty tmpfs file, from a
cgroup with memory.max=8M: the global OOM killer killed tasks owned by
root, and the machine panicked.

Fix this by creating both caches with SLAB_ACCOUNT. This change implies
that mbind() can now fail when running into memcg limits. Further,
the policy_cache also serves task and VMA policies, so they are
similarly accounted now.

Note that per-file limits are not really helpful, as the user could
simply use many files; having limits per user is tricky as well.

Fix generated by an LLM and submitted by Chris Mason in private.

summary: smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly

A 2048-byte ASCII directory name needs 4098 bytes when converted to
UTF-16, including the terminator. ksmbd_convert_dir_info_name() caps
its allocation at PATH_MAX and writes past the end of that buffer.

Allocate space for one UTF-16 code unit per input byte plus the
terminator. Use kmalloc_array() to check the size calculation.

summary: thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

thunderbolt: Do not RPM complete unrelated subtrees on unplug

When a Thunderbolt device is unplugged, that switch and every switch
subsequent to it on the bus device list is `complete()`d, not just its
child devices. In the case of multiple domains, it may cause, eg, an
attempt to `complete()` the uninitialized domain 1 root switch RPM
completion on unplug of a switch from domain 0 (though ordering is not
guaranteed numerically sorted).

I initially noticed this issue on a Dell XPS9720 when the system would
seem to sporadically not wake after unplugging a Thunderbolt dock. I
tried multiple kernel versions including v7.2.7 and v7.3-rc4 to see if
that resolved the issue, but the issue persisted. Eventually I found
that I could consistently generate a kernel Oops reporting a page fault
at 0xffff_ffff_ffff_fff8 on unplug from one side of the laptop and went
bug hunting. I became suspicious of the `bus_for_each_dev()` walk that I
ultimately ended up changing. To confirm this issue, I did an eBPF trace
of `bus_for_each_dev()`, `complete_rpm()`, and `complete()` while
unplugging in a variety of situations and found that an unplug from
domain 0 tries to `complete_rpm()` domain 1's switch, whose RPM
completion is not initialized and thus is holding a null wait-list
pointer, triggering the page fault.

Here are the key sections of that eBPF trace. Note that HEAD denotes the
completion's own wait-list HEAD:

```
RESCAN_ENTER domain=0

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=0-1 target_domain=0
         route=0x1 parent=0-0 unplugged=1
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=HEAD prev=HEAD

BUS_WALK domain=0 start=0-1 callback=complete_rpm
CALLBACK_ENTER rescan_domain=0 dev=1-0 parent=domain1 is_switch=1

COMPLETE rescan_domain=0 target=1-0 target_domain=1
         route=0x0 parent=domain1 unplugged=0
COMPLETION done=0 head=HEAD next=0 prev=0

        complete+5
        complete_rpm+43
        bus_for_each_dev+133
        icm_free_unplugged_children+250
        icm_rescan_work+42
```

This patch gates the `complete()` on an additional condition - that the
Thunderbolt domain matches the domain of the device that was unplugged.

I only have a single system with multiple Thunderbolt domains - the Dell
XPS9720. I am consistently able to reproduce the Oops on that system.
Since running with this patch, I have not seen the Oops reoccur. I have
also tested it on a Thinkpad X1-Gen12, and that system boots and runs
well with it, but it only has a single Thunderbolt domain, so it does
not exercise the multi-domain failure case.

summary: vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order
details:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost: fix used ring index wrap in vhost_add_used_n_in_order

vhost_add_used_n_in_order() advances start by nheads[i] but wraps it
with a single subtraction.  If start + nheads[i] >= 2 * vq->num, start
can remain outside the ring.

With used-ring logging enabled, start > vq->num makes (vq->num - start)
underflow.  log_write() then sets bits beyond the dirty-log bitmap,
potentially corrupting adjacent userspace memory.  This is reachable on
the vhost-net TX path with VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER: done_idx can reach
VHOST_NET_BATCH (64), triggering the issue with a 32-entry ring.

Wrap start with a mask to keep it within the ring.  VHOST_SET_VRING_NUM
enforces a nonzero power-of-two ring size, allowing start to be wrapped
using & (vq->num - 1).
